title: The Volume Rebate a Corporate Travel Programmes Programme Takes Off an Air Ticket Fare Brands Service Charge
content:
A Corporate Travel Programmes programme that has billed enough over the period read may take a rebate off the gross agency service charge raised on an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking. Two readings decide it: the programme's billing measured against its own volume rebate threshold, and whether its rebate percentage stands above zero.

## 1. The rebate

| Where | The rebate taken off the gross charge is |
| --- | --- |
| the programme's billing so read reaches its volume rebate threshold and its rebate percentage is above 0 | the programme's whole rebate percentage |
| the programme's billing so read reaches half of that threshold but not the whole of it, and its rebate percentage is above 0 | 0.5 of the programme's rebate percentage, being 50 percent of it |
| in every other case | no such rebate is taken off |

Half of the threshold means the threshold taken at 0.5. A programme whose rebate percentage stands at 0 falls to the last row whatever it has billed, because both of the first two rows turn on a percentage above zero.

## 2. Where the figures come from

The volume rebate threshold and the rebate percentage are terms of the Corporate Travel Programmes programme standing against the booking, read from that programme's own record. The billing compared against them is the programme's billing over the period read.

## 3. Boundary readings, on hypothetical figures

A programme whose volume rebate threshold is a hypothetical 40000.00 USD and whose rebate percentage is 4: billing of exactly 40000.00 USD reaches the threshold, so the whole 4 percent is taken off. Billing of 20000.00 USD reaches half of the threshold but not the whole, so 2 percent is taken off. Billing of 19000.00 USD reaches neither, and no such rebate is taken off.

The same programme with a rebate percentage of 0: billing of 60000.00 USD notwithstanding, no such rebate is taken off.
